MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.description: Modifier stacking uses TWO separate pools that never cross-apply. Prep tasks use condition+height+profile. Coating tasks use QT+height+profile. Contamination drives task activation, not rate modification.
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_prep: POOR(2.00) x H3(1.50) x Ornate(1.40) = 4.20x — slightly exceeds 4.0x flag, flag for estimator review
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.resolution: STACKING PARTITION — prep pool and coating pool never overlap. Extreme combos flagged for estimator review.

prep_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (condition x height x profile_complexity)

coating_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (qt x height x profile_complexity)

trim_surface_input_group.description: Rate per LF applies to aggregate trim LF across all in-scope items. Engine sums LF from all active trim items and divides by rate to calculate hours. Profile complexity modifiers applied per-item-type.

task_production_rates.name: Clear Furniture and Contents from Trim Work Zones
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Per-room fixed time. Lighter scope than wall RP full-room center-pile (12 min) — trim work zones are narrower, only clear items 3+ ft from walls. 5-12 min per room depending on furnishing density. Derived from wall RP TSK_WLRP_FURNITURE_MOVE (12 min) scaled down ~67% for reduced scope.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter Drops)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_FLOOR_PROTECT (300 SF/hr). Runner-style drop cloths along trim perimeter. Same task in RP — finished floors always present.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Masking at Trim Edge
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim prime TSK_SETUP_WALL_MASK (150 LF/hr). In RP, wall masking is ALWAYS required (walls are finished) for both brush (tape only) and spray (tape + paper). Rate represents spray/paper scenario as the more labor-intensive case. Brush-only tape is faster (~200 LF/hr) but rate conservatively uses spray baseline since both methods need masking.

task_production_rates.name: Cover Fixtures Near Spray Zone
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_FIXTURE_COVER (30 EA/hr). Tape over outlet/switch plates near spray zone. ~2 min per fixture. Spray method only.

task_production_rates.name: Visual Condition Scan — All Trim Surfaces

QT3.notes: Quick visual scan with work light, document visible defects per trim type

QT4.notes: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, map per trim type

QT5.notes: Critical assessment, multiple passes, raking light, full photo documentation per trim type

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Derived from wall RP TSK_WLRP_ASSESS_CONDITION (8-25 min per room for walls). Trim assessment is faster — less surface area per room but more surface types to inspect (up to 9 trim types). Scaled to ~60-70% of wall RP times. QT3=6 min (quick scan), QT4=10 min (systematic), QT5=18 min (critical).

task_production_rates.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_WLRP_ASSESS_ADHESION (8 min per room). Same ASTM D3359 procedure. Test at 2+ locations per room on different trim types. ~4 min per test site. Trim is higher risk for adhesion failure than walls due to higher sheen existing coatings.

task_production_rates.name: Coating Identification — Latex vs Oil
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_WLRP_ASSESS_COATING_ID (5 min per room). Solvent test with mineral spirits. Trim historically received oil-based paint more frequently than walls — this test is especially critical for trim RP.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Check at Suspect Areas
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from wall RP TSK_WLRP_ASSESS_MOISTURE (5 min per room for walls). Trim has less surface area but targeted check at bathroom trim, kitchen trim, window casings. Slightly faster. Active moisture = STOP WORK condition.

task_production_rates.name: Lead Test (XRF or Swab)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_RRP_LEAD_TEST (10 min per room). XRF preferred. Trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint — interior trim historically received multiple layers of lead-based oil paint.

task_production_rates.name: RRP Containment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_RRP_CONTAINMENT_SETUP (30 min per room). Poly sheeting on floors and openings, warning signs, restrict access. EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

task_production_rates.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_RRP_HEPA_VACUUM (20 min per room). HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance. Required by EPA RRP Rule.

task_production_rates.name: RRP Containment Removal and Visual Clearance
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_RRP_CONTAINMENT_REMOVAL (20 min per room). Remove containment poly, visual clearance inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Lead-Contaminated Waste Disposal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. DIRECT transfer from wall RP TSK_RRP_WASTE_DISPOSAL (30 min per job). Package and dispose lead-contaminated debris per EPA RRP Rule.

task_production_rates.name: TSP Wash Trim Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from wall RP TSK_WLRP_WASH_TSP (250 SF/hr for walls). Trim TSP wash is slower per LF than walls per SF — profile detail areas require rag work into crevices. 150 LF/hr baseline. Prep pool modifiers apply. Contamination type drives task activation, not rate modification.

task_production_rates.name: Mildew/Biocide Treatment on Trim
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from wall RP TSK_WLRP_TREAT_MILDEW (200 SF/hr for walls). Trim mildew treatment slower per LF — apply solution into profile detail, allow dwell, rinse. Includes dwell time. 120 LF/hr baseline. Source moisture must already be resolved.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Existing Trim Paint Surface

QT3.notes: Thorough degloss — chemical or mechanical, all accessible surfaces

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification on profiled surfaces (160 / 1.3)

QT5.notes: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test (160 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from NC trim sand rate TSK_TRIM_SAND_PREP (200 LF/hr). Degloss is ~80% of NC sand rate — chemical degloss requires wipe-on/wipe-off cycle, mechanical scuff on profiles uses contour sponge. 160 LF/hr baseline at QT3. Prep pool modifiers apply. Chemical degloss preferred for profiled trim — reaches crevices that sanding blocks cannot.

task_production_rates.name: Scrape Loose and Failing Paint from Trim

QT3.notes: Remove all failing paint, thorough scrape of affected areas

QT4.notes: Comprehensive scrape, careful profile work, identify all weak adhesion zones (45 / 1.3)

QT5.notes: Critical scrape — near-zero tolerance for remaining loose material (45 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Slow detail work — contour scraper follows molding profiles, putty knife for flat runs. 45 LF/hr baseline at QT3. Significantly slower than wall scraping (wall RP 80 SF/hr) because trim profiles create more detailed work per LF. Prep pool modifiers apply. FAIR/POOR condition only — GOOD condition skips scraping.

task_production_rates.name: Feather-Sand Scrape Edges on Trim

QT3.notes: Smooth transition, no visible ridge at 6 ft

QT4.notes: Near-invisible transition, no ridge at 3 ft (80 / 1.3)

QT5.notes: Perfect transition, no ridge at arm's length (80 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Feather-sand all scrape edges to prevent ridge telegraphing. Contour sanding sponge for profiled trim. 80 LF/hr baseline at QT3 — faster than scraping but still detail work. Non-negotiable at all tiers. Prep pool modifiers apply. Always follows TSK_TMRP_SCRAPE_LOOSE.

task_production_rates.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk on Trim Joints

QT3.notes: Replace visibly failed sections — cracked or separated joints

QT4.notes: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints (80 / 1.3)

QT5.notes: Critical assessment, replace all joints not in perfect condition, perfect tooled bead (80 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from NC trim caulk TSK_TRIM_CAULK_JOINTS (135 LF/hr for full NC caulk). RP caulk assess/replace is ~60% of NC full-caulk rate — includes inspection walk (which joints need work?), removal of failed sections, and replacement. Estimated 15-30% of joints need replacement in typical RP. 80 LF/hr baseline at QT3. Prep pool modifiers apply.

task_production_rates.name: Dust Wipe Trim Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim prime TSK_TRIM_DUST_WIPE (300 LF/hr). Wipe with tack cloth per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12. Binary task — surface is dust-free or it is not. Same standard all tiers.

task_production_rates.name: Brush State-Driven Primer on Trim

QT3.notes: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays

QT5.notes: Complete coverage, no visible brush marks, uniform film (90 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim prime TSK_TRIM_PRIME_BRUSH (90 LF/hr at QT3). State-driven primer has similar application characteristics to NC primer — same brush, same pace. Primer product varies by substrate state (adhesion, mildew, stain-block) but application rate is consistent. Skip for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion passes.

task_production_rates.name: Spray State-Driven Primer on Trim

QT3.notes: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays

QT5.notes: Complete coverage, perfect uniformity, no orange peel (375 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim prime TSK_TRIM_PRIME_SPRAY (375 LF/hr at QT3). Spray application rate independent of primer type. Skip for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion passes.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Prime Scraped/Repaired Areas

QT3.notes: Spot prime all repair areas, sealed against flashing

QT4.notes: Spot prime all repairs with feathered edges (120 / 1.3)

QT5.notes: Spot prime all repairs with wide feather, may need light sand after (120 / 1.5)

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Walk rate — brush spot prime on scraped areas, feathered edges, and caulk replacements. Prevents flashing from differential absorption. Faster than full prime (brush at 120 vs 90 LF/hr) because only localized areas need attention. Rate is per aggregate trim LF (walk rate). Used for GOOD condition or to supplement full prime at repair areas.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_INSPECT_COAT (QT3=800, QT4=500, QT5=300 LF/hr). Same inspection protocol in RP — inspection rigor and rates are independent of NC vs RP context. Per Fine Finish Doctrine.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Between Coats

QT3.notes: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit.

QT4.notes: Light full sand — entire surface, 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.

QT5.notes: Thorough full sand — entire surface, 220-320 grit. Every imperfection addressed.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_SAND_BETWEEN (QT3=400, QT4=250, QT5=150 LF/hr). Between-coat sanding uses contour sanding sponge for profiles. Coating pool modifiers apply. Per Fine Finish Doctrine 15.4.1.

task_production_rates.name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Repair glaring defects only — deep scratches, obvious holes

QT4.notes: Repair all marked defects — visible at 3 feet

QT5.notes: Repair all defects regardless of size — anything that could telegraph through finish

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_PATCH_DEFECTS (QT3=400, QT4=300, QT5=250 LF/hr). Same interstage patch process in RP. Walk rate — most LF requires no patching at QT3. Coating pool modifiers apply.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas

QT5.notes: Spot coat all repairs — ensure uniform film build

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_SPOT_COAT (QT3=500, QT4=380, QT5=300 LF/hr). Same interstage spot coat process in RP. Walk rate. Coating pool modifiers apply.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_CLEAN_INTERSTAGE (600 LF/hr). Tack cloth wipe all sanded trim surfaces between coats. ~6 sec per LF. Binary — complete dust removal is same pace at all tiers.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat 1

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_BRUSH_FINISH_1 (80 LF/hr). Coat 1 is slower than coat 2 — surface absorption, establishing coverage. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Application quality is binary, not tiered.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat 1

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_SPRAY_FINISH_1 (380 LF/hr). Coat 1 airless spray. Application quality is binary, not tiered.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat 2

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_BRUSH_FINISH_2 (90 LF/hr). Coat 2 faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate. Also used for coat 3 at QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat 2

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_SPRAY_FINISH_2 (445 LF/hr). Coat 2 faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate.

task_production_rates.name: Final Trim Inspection

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects, uniform sheen

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — no visible defects, uniform sheen across all surfaces

QT5.notes: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, gallery-quality finish

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_FINAL_INSPECT (QT3=600, QT4=400, QT5=250 LF/hr). Slower than interstage inspect — final inspection is more thorough even at QT3. Same protocol in RP.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Defects (Final)

QT4.notes: Address all visible defects — blend touch-up into surrounding finish

QT5.notes: Address every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed to equalize sheen

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_TOUCHUP (QT3=400, QT4=300, QT5=200 LF/hr). Same touch-up process in RP. Walk rate with spot work. Coating pool modifiers apply.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Wall Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim prime TSK_REMOVE_WALL_MASK (200 LF/hr). Teardown is ~33% faster than setup. Remove tape while finish is slightly tacky for cleanest pull. Both brush and spray methods require teardown in RP.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Fixture Covers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from NC trim prime TSK_REMOVE_FIXTURE_COVERS (90 EA/hr in NC prime spec). Rate adjusted to 45 EA/hr — teardown is faster than setup but NC prime rate of 90 EA/hr was for an earlier spec with simpler fixture count assumption. 45 EA/hr = ~80 sec per fixture (remove cover, inspect, dispose).

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_PROTECT_TEARDOWN (500 SF/hr). Fold drops toward center to contain debris. Teardown ~1.5x faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Restore Furniture and Contents to Original Position
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Per-room fixed time. Return furniture to original positions. Faster than clear (6 vs 8 min) — no decisions about where to move, just return. Verify no paint transfer. Lighter scope than wall RP because trim work zones are narrower.

task_production_rates.name: Customer Walkthrough
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Walk each room with homeowner. Inspect trim finish quality at all trim types. Identify any touch-up needs. Confirm completion. 5 min per room includes discussion. Lead skill level — crew lead or project manager handles client interaction.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from NC trim paint TSK_TRIM_CLEAN_TOOLS (30 min per session). Fixed time per job session. Clean brushes, spray equipment (if used). All waterborne products — water cleanup. RP may include additional cleanup for deglosser/TSP supplies.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Time multiplier based on quality tier selection per Modifier_Registry.md
factor_modifiers.notes: QT modifiers increase TIME, not rate. Applied to qt_scaled tasks only. Binary tasks unaffected. Coating pool only — never stacks with condition modifier.

factor_modifiers.name: Condition Scale Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Time multiplier based on surface condition (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine
factor_modifiers.notes: Prep pool only — never stacks with QT modifier. Drives prep task intensity. Shared with wall RP.

factor_modifiers.name: Profile Complexity Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Time multiplier based on trim profile complexity per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2
factor_modifiers.applies_to_tasks: prep and finish tasks with LF input_group
factor_modifiers.notes: Shared across both prep and coating pools. Applied per-item-type (baseboard may be simple, crown may be complex). Inherited from NC trim FAC_PROFILE_COMPLEXITY.

factor_modifiers.name: Height Modifier for Trim
factor_modifiers.description: Time multiplier based on trim working height per Modifier_Registry.md
factor_modifiers.applies_to_tasks: all tasks except FIXED time and EA tasks

height_ranges.H2_TALL: 9-12ft — step/extension ladder for crown, high casings
height_ranges.H3_HIGH: 13-17ft — scaffold likely for elevated trim work

factor_modifiers.notes: Shared across both prep and coating pools. Primarily affects crown molding and high casing work. Standard baseboard/casing at floor level uses H1. H4 excluded for interior trim. Per-item-type: baseboard=H1, crown/picture_rail=H2/H3.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard trim repaint — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard RP production: proper prep, conditional prime, 2 finish coats. Quick glance inspection at 6ft.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium trim repaint — thorough prep, full interstage sanding
quality_tier_effects.notes: Premium: detailed inspection, all visible defects addressed, full surface between-coat sanding. Semi-gloss minimum sheen.

quality_tier_effects.description: Superior trim repaint — meticulous prep, critical inspection, optional coat 3 brush
quality_tier_effects.notes: Superior: meticulous pace, every defect addressed, thorough 220-320 grit sanding. Coat count: 2 (spray) or 3 (brush per FFD 15.10.3). Gloss sheen allowed.

additional_rounds.description: QT5 brush adds coat 3 + interstage 2. Coat 3 uses TSK_TMRP_BRUSH_FINISH_2 rates (consistent substrate). Per FFD 15.10.3.
additional_rounds.notes: Applies to both ROUND_TMRP_PRIME_3FINISH (FAIR/POOR) and ROUND_TMRP_3FINISH (GOOD). Do NOT enforce spray for QT5 gloss.

round_configurations.name: Trim RP: Prime + 3 Finish Coats (QT5 Brush)
Trim RP: 3 Finish Coats (QT5 Brush, No Prime)

crew_configurations.name: Single Trim Brush Painter (RP)
crew_configurations.notes: One journeyman handles assessment, all prep, prime, and finish. Helper for setup/teardown/furniture. Lead for customer walkthrough.

crew_configurations.name: Single Trim Sprayer (RP)
crew_configurations.notes: One journeyman handles assessment, prep, masking, spray, teardown. Helper for setup. Lead for customer walkthrough.

production_notes.rate_derivation_strategy: Three-tier derivation: (1) DIRECT transfer from NC trim for same-process tasks (protection, finish coats, interstage, cleanup, inspection). (2) MODIFIED from NC trim for adjusted-scope tasks (degloss from sand, caulk assess from full caulk). (3) RP-NEW for assessment and condition-dependent tasks, derived from wall RP patterns adapted to LF context.
production_notes.lf_to_sf_equivalence: Per PDCA standard, 1 LF trim = 1 SF regardless of actual width (Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 1.3).
production_notes.condition_vs_qt: Condition modifiers (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) drive prep pool intensity. QT modifiers drive coating pool scrutiny. They NEVER cross-apply. This prevents double-compounding on the same task.
production_notes.profile_complexity_note: Profile complexity applied per-item-type — baseboard may be simple while crown may be ornate in the same project. Engine must apply modifier per item, not globally.
production_notes.coat_1_vs_coat_2: Coat 1 is systematically slower than coat 2 (surface absorption vs consistent substrate). Separate task IDs enable distinct rates. Coat 3 at QT5 uses coat 2 rates.
production_notes.rp_vs_nc_differences: Key RP additions vs NC: (1) Assessment module (4 tasks). (2) Furniture clear/restore. (3) Customer walkthrough. (4) Condition-driven prep (degloss, scrape, feather). (5) State-driven primer selection. (6) RRP lead-safe module. (7) Wall masking always-on for both methods.

assumptions.value: 8 min per room (lighter scope than wall RP 12 min)
assumptions.source: Derived from wall RP TSK_WLRP_FURNITURE_MOVE, scaled ~67%
assumptions.note: Trim work zones are narrower — only items within 3 ft of walls need clearing, not full room center-pile.

assumptions.value: 160 LF/hr (80% of NC sand rate 200 LF/hr)
assumptions.source: Derived from NC trim TSK_TRIM_SAND_PREP baseline
assumptions.note: Chemical degloss wipe-on/wipe-off cycle is similar effort to mechanical scuffing. 80% factor accounts for chemical application/dwell/wipe vs direct sanding.

assumptions.value: 80 LF/hr (~60% of NC full-caulk rate 135 LF/hr)
assumptions.source: Derived from NC trim TSK_TRIM_CAULK_JOINTS baseline
assumptions.note: RP caulk assess/replace includes inspection walk + selective removal + replacement. 15-30% of joints need replacement in typical RP.

assumptions.source: Calibrated from wall RP scrape (80 SF/hr) adjusted for trim profile complexity
assumptions.note: Trim scraping with contour scraper is slower per LF than wall scraping per SF — profile detail work.

assumptions.source: Calibrated: faster than scraping, slower than between-coat sanding
assumptions.note: Feathering requires smooth transitions at scrape edges — detail work with contour sanding sponge.

assumptions.value: Condition 6-18 min, adhesion 8 min, coating ID 5 min, moisture 4 min per room
assumptions.source: Derived from wall RP assessment times, scaled for trim surface area
assumptions.note: Trim assessment faster than wall assessment — less surface area per room but more surface types to inspect.

assumptions.value: Coat 3 at QT5 brush uses same rates as coat 2 (TSK_TMRP_BRUSH_FINISH_2 at 90 LF/hr)
assumptions.source: Production Rate Reference System 3, same as NC convention
assumptions.note: No separate coat 3 rate defined. Coat 2 rates apply — substrate is consistent after first coat.

validation_plan.method: Time chemical degloss on 50 LF baseboard (standard profile) and 50 LF crown (complex profile)
validation_plan.notes: Verify chemical vs mechanical degloss rate differential.

validation_plan.method: Time contour scraping on 50 LF failing paint trim, FAIR condition
validation_plan.notes: Verify trim profile impact vs flat wall scraping.

validation_plan.method: Walk 100 LF trim joints, count and time assessment + selective replacement
validation_plan.notes: Verify ~15-30% replacement assumption. Count actual failed joints.

validation_plan.method: Time full assessment sequence (condition + adhesion + coating ID + moisture) in 5 rooms
validation_plan.expected_range: 20-35 min total per room at QT3
validation_plan.notes: Verify task-level time estimates sum to realistic total.

validation_plan.method: Time painter brushing finish coat on 100 LF previously painted trim
validation_plan.notes: Verify NC rates transfer cleanly to RP context. Compare coat 1 vs coat 2 differential.

validation_plan.method: Time furniture clear and restore in 5 typical rooms with standard furnishing
validation_plan.expected_range: Clear 5-12 min, Restore 4-10 min per room
validation_plan.notes: Verify lighter scope than wall RP full-room center-pile.
